name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+21 partisan lean makes a Democratic win near-certain in the general election
Jasmine Clark holds a massive financial edge: $2.3 million raised and $4.2 million in outside support versus no reported fundraising for Jonathan Chavez
Open seat after the Democratic primary, which was the true contest in this deep-blue district
Prediction markets price Democratic victory at roughly 98 percent
model.rationale: The district's D+21 lean, Clark's overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and Chavez's lack of any visible campaign resources leave no realistic path for a Republican upset; the competitive phase of this race ended with the Democratic primary.
model.watch: The outcome is highly unlikely to change, but the size of Clark's margin could shift with turnout levels and any late-breaking developments in the campaign.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District, anchored in Atlanta's southern suburbs, is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward Democrats. David Scott's departure set off a competitive Democratic primary that Jasmine Clark won, effectively settling the race in this deep-blue district. Everton Blair is not on the ballot for the full term.

Clark enters the general election with a major financial edge: about $2.3 million raised and more than $4.2 million in outside support, while Republican Jonathan Chavez reports no fundraising. No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have weighed in, but prediction markets put Democratic chances near 98 percent. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the real question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
